evidence:
Read cold, instruction.md is a first-person team request in prose paragraphs with no numbered acceptance list, no spec table, no feature matrix and no bullets (grep for list/table markers on the file returns nothing). It opens with a product framing and a stated pain point: instruction.md:1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Requirements are phrased as user needs, not acceptance clauses: instruction.md:3 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who.'; instruction.md:5 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor'; instruction.md:7 'leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone and just tell me there is something new.' It explicitly leaves design and layout to the builder: instruction.md:11 'layout and names are yours. A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' 'must' appears only twice (instruction.md:9 'They must never see our internal notes', instruction.md:13 'It must start with node /app/server.js'), both in natural sentences, not a shall/must table.

Build-recipe test: instruction.md:13 names the stack (Node.js, Express, SQLite), entry, port, health route, DB path and DB_PATH. That is not a task-authored build recipe: it restates the template-mandated runtime contract in the frozen template's environment/instructions/integration.md:3-10 (Node 22, Express, better-sqlite3, /app/server.js, port 3000, /app/app.db, DB_PATH, GET /api/health), which row 4 requires the brief to state. It names exactly one endpoint (the mandated health check), and explicitly refuses to prescribe file layout or routes: instruction.md:13 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Line 17's account list is required identity data, also phrased conversationally ('Everyone signs in with password Hireops!2026'). Line 11 delegates exact rules to /instructions/hireops_rules.md the way a team would point at its working-rules doc.

Companion note observation (not a defect for this row): hireops_rules.md is denser and more spec-like (role table at :14-19, stage-wording table at :182-189, bullet rules, HTTP codes 401/403/404/409 at :21-23 and :78, 'Follow them exactly' at :3). Row 1's procedure targets instruction.md ('read instruction.md cold'), and a team rules note with tables is a plausible real artefact; it also explicitly disclaims a recipe at :3-5 ('Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours'). Whether the note's voice/consistency is acceptable belongs to row 2 (voice change between instruction.md and notes) and row 5/6, not this row.

Adversarial checks for this row: (a) a broken app cannot pass because of the instruction's naturalness; this row grades prompt form only, so a weak app's score is not affected by this verdict. (b) A conforming alternative is not pushed into a hidden shape by the brief: the brief names no routes beyond /api/health, no element ids, no view names ('layout and names are yours'), and no file layout, so a builder with different routes, names or drag/no-drag control style is still conforming per the prompt; whether criteria respect that is rows 27/32, outside this assignment. No runtime evidence is required for this row (static prose judgement); none was claimed. Not checked here: raw-evidence-index hashes, since no runtime claim underpins this verdict.
